data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Avram means 'father of a multitude'. In the Bible, this name is given to Abraham, the patriarch of the Jewish people. God promised Abraham that he would be the father of many nations. The name Avrom carries the meaning “Father of a multitude” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Avrom usually hope their child will grow to embody father of a multitude and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avrom total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

The name Avrom is commonly used in modern Christian cultures, reflecting the values of family, loyalty, and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: Avram, or Abraham, is prominent in several religions, including Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. His story is well known for his revered status as the patriarch of the Jewish people, and his deep faith and obedience to God. The name Avram carries with it a rich cultural heritage, representing sacrifice, obedience, and the longing for a deeper, spiritual connection with God.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Avram (Abraham) is a revered figure, praised for his unwavering faith and obedience to God. He is known for his trust in God's promises, and his willingness to sacrifice his only son, Isaac, as a test of his obedience. Avram's name carries spiritual significance as a reminder of God's promise to bless those who trust and obey Him. The name Avram is a reminder of the importance of faith, obedience, and the covenant relationship between God and His people.
